clue.text: Puts cheap material into cobbles

indicators.note: the letters of the first two words are the raw material, worked into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A cobbler tucks cheap leather into the shoes being mended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material into' signals that PUTS CHEAP is reworked into a new order; 'cobbles' is the verb meaning mends roughly, not the paving stones.
explanation.definitionFit: To cobble something is to repair it clumsily or hastily, the same as a makeshift mend.

clue.text: Cereal food — finished article

parts.note: something finished is over and done, past
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A breakfast cereal is offered as a finished item for sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is made from durum wheat, a cereal grain, so it counts as a cereal food.

clue.text: Aid for climbers crossing bars

explanation.surface: Something helps mountaineers get across a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden lattice supports climbing plants, and it is built of laths that cross one another.

clue.text: Queen Catherine's relations escort me to my house

indicators.note: relations who escort someone walk on either side, so they surround the next word

parts.note: Catherine Howard was a wife of Henry VIII, so her relations are the Howards
taken as written

explanation.surface: A queen's family accompany the speaker back to the speaker's own home.
explanation.walkthrough: Catherine Howard, fifth wife of Henry VIII, gives the family name HOWARDS; 'escort' puts ME inside it, HO-ME-WARDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading in the direction of one's own home is moving towards it, a direction adverb.

clue.text: Season wood as basis for vaulting

parts.note: spring is one of the four seasons
a board is a piece of wood

explanation.surface: Timber is seasoned as the foundation for an arched roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vaulting' suggests the arched ceiling the wood might support, but it is gymnastic leaping; 'Season' looks like a verb (to dry timber) but gives the season SPRING.
explanation.definitionFit: Gymnasts launch a vault from a flexible board that gives them lift, the base of the jump.

clue.text: Sire has right standard of course

parts.note: a sire is a father, informally pa

explanation.surface: A father naturally has the right standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as 'naturally', but it means of a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course the expected number of strokes for a hole is the benchmark score.

clue.text: Was a knight so loudly hailed?

definitions.text: Was a knight so loudly hailed?

parts.words: Was a knight so loudly hailed?
parts.note: a knight began as a boy attendant in a household before being dubbed; being summoned over a loudspeaker is the modern way to be hailed loudly, and the verb covers both

explanation.surface: A question about whether a knight was greeted with loud cheering.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb has two readings: to have served as a young attendant on the road to knighthood, and to be called for by name over a public-address system.
explanation.definitionFit: Being summoned by name over a tannoy is the modern sense; serving as a boy attendant before knighthood is the old one.

clue.text: Tom's father produces play chosen by financial backer

definitions.text: produces play chosen by financial backer

explanation.surface: A boy's dad stages a show picked by its investor.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme runs 'Tom, Tom, the piper's son'; the proverb 'he who pays the piper calls the tune' gives the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme Tom's dad was a musician; in the proverb the musician plays whatever tune the paymaster chooses.

clue.text: He makes light of gap in wall

definitions.text: He makes light of gap in wall

parts.words: He makes light of gap in wall
parts.note: making light of something usually means treating it as trivial, but here it means letting daylight through the opening of a window

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a hole in the wall as nothing serious.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who fits panes of glass into window frames lets light through the openings in walls.

clue.text: Send-off for boy raised on prayer-book

indicators.note: in a down clue a word raised is read upwards, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: Sid is a boy's name
a missal is a book of prayers for Mass

explanation.surface: A boy is given a farewell party after being brought up on the prayer book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns SID upward into DIS, which sits on top of MISSAL in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A send-off can be a sacking or, in sport, an ordering off the field, both a removal.

clue.text: Kitchen craft ?

parts.note: looks like the skill of cooking, but craft is a vessel and kitchen names a cooking pan, so the words describe both a pan for cooking with vapour and a boat

explanation.surface: A question about the art of cookery.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a pan that cooks food in vapour and a ship powered by boiler-driven engines.

clue.text: Salesman chews over second orders

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
to chew is to eat

explanation.surface: A salesman munches through a second round of orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeat orders are further orders for the same goods, a second batch of the same request.

clue.text: Let gangster down

parts.note: Al Capone was the archetypal gangster
feeling down is feeling low

explanation.surface: Someone lets a gangster down.
explanation.walkthrough: AL is the crossword's standard gangster, after Al Capone.
explanation.definitionFit: To let someone do something is to permit it.

clue.text: Fit entire ensemble for beauty queen

indicators.note: an ensemble is an outfit put together, so the letters of the two words are assembled anew

explanation.surface: A complete outfit is chosen to suit a pageant winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ensemble' asks for FIT ENTIRE to be put together in a new order; 'beauty queen' is no pageant winner but an Egyptian queen famed for her looks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian queen, wife of Akhenaten, is famous for her painted bust and legendary beauty.

clue.text: Corps in wrong location

parts.note: corps is French for body, and something in the wrong place is alien to it, as with a speck in the eye

explanation.surface: An army corps has been deployed to the wrong place.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors use the term for an object lodged in the body that does not belong there, such as a splinter.

clue.text: Relative — the one that's embarked

annotationWithheld.why: Relative—the one that's embarked (3): SIS is I (one) inside SS, but the only word for SS is 'embarked', which is also the container indicator, so one word does two jobs

clue.text: Stop as lions come out

indicators.note: out means out of order, so the letters of the lions and the word come are rearranged

explanation.surface: Halt, because the lions are coming out of their cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' signals that LIONS COME is rearranged; 'Stop' looks like a command but is a punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A punctuation mark is traditionally called a stop, and this one marks a pause stronger than a comma.

clue.text: Browning? His namesake overdoes the sunbathing

parts.note: the poet Browning's first name was Robert
someone who stays out in the sun too long burns

explanation.surface: Someone browning on the beach overdoes it and gets scorched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Browning' looks like tanning, matching the sunbathing, but it is the Victorian poet Robert Browning.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish poet shared a first name with Browning, making him Browning's namesake.

clue.text: Pseudo-aesthetic character of opera

parts.note: the words describe a figure in Gilbert and Sullivan's Patience, a sham aesthete poet satirising the aesthetic movement

explanation.surface: A fake arty type appears in an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's Patience features a 'fleshly poet' who poses as an aesthete, a caricature of Wilde's circle.

clue.text: Interference with position of secret agent

explanation.surface: Someone meddles with where a spy is stationed.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as MOLE STATION: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Harassment or meddling is interference; a planted spy's post is where that agent is stationed.

clue.text: Seductive rock-singer

parts.note: suggests a sexy pop star, but it is the siren of Rhine legend who sang from a rock and lured boatmen to their deaths

explanation.surface: A sultry rock music vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: German legend tells of a maiden on a cliff above the Rhine whose song drew sailors onto the rocks.

clue.text: Instrument that bores everyone hearing it

indicators.note: what follows is how the word for everyone strikes the ear, not how it is written

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: A musical instrument so dull it bores everyone who hears it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument that bores' suggests a tedious musical instrument; it is a tool that bores holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed hand tool used to pierce holes in leather or wood.

clue.text: Taken on as premises

explanation.surface: Something has been taken on in the form of property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'premises' looks like buildings but means propositions taken for granted in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A role or debt adopted is taken up; a proposition supposed true for argument's sake is taken for granted.

clue.text: Continued flirting?

explanation.surface: Did the flirting go on?
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going is to proceed without stopping; to have an affair is a colloquial sense of the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: Epic outcome of war over seizure of Paris

definitions.text: Epic outcome of war over seizure of Paris

parts.words: Epic outcome of war over seizure of Paris
parts.note: Paris is the Trojan prince who carried off Helen, not the French capital, and the war fought over that abduction produced Homer's poem

explanation.surface: A grand result of a war about the capture of the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris' suggests the city taken in war; it is the Trojan prince whose seizure of Helen started the Trojan War.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem tells of the Trojan War, sparked when Paris abducted Helen of Sparta.

clue.text: Wearing stockings, head of house does badly

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
done badly, the letters of the next word are muddled

explanation.surface: A house's head wears stockings and performs poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' turns DOES into OSED, which follows H from 'head of house'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hose is an old word for stockings, so someone wearing them is clad in hose.

clue.text: Unusual drain in foreign currency

indicators.note: the letters of the word drain appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An odd outflow of foreign money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drain' suggests a drain on currency reserves, but it is just the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The monetary unit of several countries, such as Iraq, Jordan and Serbia.

clue.text: £50 one got in protracted lazy lounging

indicators.note: the pieces before these words are put inside the word for protracted

parts.note: something protracted is drawn out, long
the pound sign is L (libra) and L is the Roman numeral fifty
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Fifty pounds was spent on a long idle lie-about.
explanation.walkthrough: £50 gives LL: the pound sign is L, from Latin libra, and fifty is Roman L; with I, the one, they go inside LONG.
explanation.definitionFit: To loll is to lie or sit in a relaxed, idle way, lazy lounging.

clue.text: Young woman, so it was said, gives short measure

definitions.text: Young woman, so it was said

explanation.surface: A girl, people claimed, gives customers short measure.
explanation.walkthrough: The informal word is a spoken form of 'girl'; it is also the short form of gallon.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial word for a girl, as some pronounce it, and the abbreviation of gallon, a unit of measure.

clue.text: He makes progress retrospectively

parts.note: retrospectively usually means looking back in time, but here it means facing backwards while moving forwards, as a rower does

explanation.surface: Someone advances by looking back on the past.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower sits facing the stern and so moves the boat forward while looking back.

clue.text: Nymph glimpsed in Vienna I adore her

indicators.note: only part of the words is seen, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A water spirit is seen in the Austrian capital by an admirer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a water nymph living in a spring, river or lake.

clue.text: He provides service but lacks orders

definitions.text: He provides service but lacks orders

parts.words: He provides service but lacks orders
parts.note: service is a church service and orders are holy orders, so this is someone who leads worship without being ordained

explanation.surface: A waiter serves but has received no orders.
explanation.definitionFit: A layman licensed by the Church to conduct some services without being ordained a priest.
